# Magnet Creates Pull Animation

## Problem statement

When the Magnet power-up (P9) is active, nearby power-up drops are pulled toward the ship at `MAGNET_ATTRACTION_SPEED`, but the visual representation (the `graphics` object) does not update its position — only the logical `x`/`y` coordinates change. The player cannot see the magnet pulling power-ups in, making the effect feel invisible and unintuitive.

## Users

- **Players** — want to visually see the magnet effect: drops should visibly slide toward the ship along a direct path, changing direction when the ship moves.
- **Developers** — need the animation to be consistent with the existing simulation step (`tick(dt)`) and the current magnet attraction math.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want to see power-up drops visibly slide toward my ship when the Magnet is active, so I can understand the range and strength of the effect.
- As a **player**, I want the pull direction to update in real time when I move, so the animation feels responsive and natural.
- As a **developer**, I want the visual position to stay in sync with the logical drop position used by the collection logic.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Visual sync:** Every frame, each drop's `graphics` object position is set to the drop's current `x`/`y` coordinates so the player sees the drop move.
- **AC2 — Direct path pull:** Drops within magnet range move along the shortest path toward the ship (already handled by the existing `_applyMagnet` logic computing `dx`/`dy` and stepping toward the player).
- **AC3 — Direction updates:** If the player moves while a drop is being pulled, the drop changes direction to follow the ship (the `dx`/`dy` calculation each frame naturally handles this).
- **AC4 — Existing tests pass:** The existing magnet test (`'applies the P9 magnet effect, and the magnet pulls a drop toward the ship'`) continues to pass, asserting `drop.x` moves toward the ship.
- **AC5 — Full project test suite passes.**

## Constraints

- The change must be minimal — touch only the visual position sync, do not alter magnet math, radius, or attraction speed.
- The animation must stay deterministic (same `tick(dt)` semantics — no frame-rate-dependent animation easing).
- No new Phaser dependencies or particle systems.

## Existing state

- `_applyMagnet(dt)` in `GymPowerUps.ts` correctly updates `drop.x` and `drop.y` each frame when magnet stacks > 0.
- `advanceDrops(dt)` updates `drop.graphics.setScale(drop.powerUp.currentScale)` but does NOT update the graphics position.
- `graphics.setPosition(x, y)` is called only once at spawn time — never during magnet attraction.
- The result: drops move logically (test assertions on `drop.x` pass) but appear stationary (the graphics stays at spawn position).

## Desired change

Update the graphics position each frame to reflect the current logical drop position. The correct approach is to add `drop.graphics.setPosition(drop.x, drop.y)` inside the magnet attraction loop in `_applyMagnet`, after each drop's `x`/`y` is updated — this ensures the visual position follows the logical position in the same iteration. An alternative is a dedicated `_syncDropPositions()` call after `_applyMagnet` in `tick()`, but the loop-local approach is more efficient (only updates drops within magnet range).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUps.ts` — Add `drop.graphics.setPosition(drop.x, drop.y)` in the `advanceDrops` method (or in the magnet attraction loop).

## Related work

- **AH-0MT7VE4SX0005A8V** — Add a Magnet power up (GDD spec; completed).
- **AH-0MTCNYWDO007B6CJ** — Unit tests: power-up effects, refresh & magnet math (completed; tests assert `drop.x` moves toward ship).
- **AH-0MTCO0M3C002Y67S** — GymPowerUps scene wiring (completed; implements `_applyMagnet`).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** Keep to position sync only — do not add particle trails, glow effects, or easing animations. These are nice-to-have but belong in separate items.
- **Assumption:** The existing `drop.x`/`drop.y` logic in `_applyMagnet` is correct (it is tested and audited). Only the visual sync is missing.
- **Assumption:** Updating position in `advanceDrops` is the right place — it runs after magnet attraction and before collection, keeping the visual pipeline tidy.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Should the pull animation be smooth/eased or snap to the logical position each frame?" — Answer (derived from context): Snap to logical position each `tick(dt)` step, matching the existing deterministic simulation model. No easing or interpolation needed. Source: the codebase uses deterministic `tick(dt)` steps throughout.
- Q2: "Should any visual effect accompany the pull (particle trail, glow intensification)?" — Answer: Not for this work item. The operator's brief is about making the effect visible, not decorative. Decorative extras are scope-creep.

# Make weapons cumulative and time out

## Headline

Replace the persistent weapon system with a cumulative, time-limited model: collecting a weapon power-up adds its firing effects to the ship's arsenal for 10 seconds, while the initial cannon remains permanent.

## Problem statement

The current weapon system uses a single-slot persistent model — collecting a weapon power-up **replaces** the currently equipped weapon with no timer. The operator has requested that weapons be **cumulative** (stacking effects) and **time out** after 10 seconds, with the exception of the initial cannon.

## Users

- **Player testing the game** — wants to collect multiple weapon power-ups and see their firing effects stack, then watch them expire one-by-one over 10 seconds, creating a dynamic and escalating combat experience.
- **Developer implementing the change** — needs a clear model for tracking multiple active weapons with individual timers and updating the Player entity, GymWeapons scene, and weapon utilities to support this behavior.

## Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want to collect Spread while already firing the cannon so my ship fires *both* patterns, giving me more coverage without replacing my existing weapon.
- As a **player**, I want to see weapons I've collected time out after 10 seconds so that combat feels dynamic and power-ups create temporary bursts of capability rather than permanent upgrades.
- As a **player**, I want the initial cannon to **never time out** so I always have at least one reliable weapon.
- As a **player**, I want the Reset power-up to clear all timed weapons and leave only the cannon, giving me a way to "refresh" if I've lost all my timed weapons.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Cumulative weapons:** The Player entity tracks a **collection** of active weapons instead of a single equipped weapon. Collecting a weapon power-up adds it to the active set (no replacement). The cannon is always present in the active set.
- [ ] **AC2 — 10-second timeout per weapon:** Each weapon power-up (spread, dual, rapid) gets its own independent 10-second countdown from the moment of collection. When a timed weapon expires, it is removed from the active set and stops firing. The cannon has no timer and never expires.
- [ ] **AC3 — Auto-fire all active weapons:** On each fire cycle, the ship fires from **every active weapon** in the collection simultaneously. Each weapon fires at its own fire rate independently (e.g., rapid fires every 125ms, cannon every 400ms, spread every 600ms).
- [ ] **AC4 — Reset power-up clears timed weapons:** Collecting the Reset power-up removes all timed weapons (spread, dual, rapid) from the active set, leaving only the permanent cannon. The Reset power-up itself is not a weapon and is never added to the active set.
- [ ] **AC5 — GymWeapons scene updated:** The GymWeapons scene correctly handles the new cumulative model — collecting drops adds weapons to the active set, the Reset drop clears timed weapons, expired weapons are silently dropped, and auto-fire fires from all active weapons.
- [ ] **AC6 — Testing:** Unit tests verify: weapon collection adds to active set, individual weapon timers count down and expire, expired weapons are removed, cannon never expires, Reset clears all timed weapons, auto-fire emits bullets from all active weapons at correct rates. Full suite green.
- [ ] **AC7 — Documentation:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the cumulative + timed weapon semantics (GDD §4.4 revision, code comments, README).
- [ ] **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Engine/stack:** Phaser v4 + TypeScript, Vite, Vitest (locked). Neon-vector aesthetic.
- **Threat-free gym:** no enemies, no enemy bullets, no collision damage — player bullets are demonstration-only.
- **Backward compatibility:** the GymWeapons scene must continue to work with the new model.
- **Existing code to refactor:** Player.ts (single `_equippedWeapon` → weapon collection with timers), weapons.ts (add timeout tracking helpers if needed), GymWeapons.ts (collection logic update).

## Existing state

- `Player.ts` (`src/entities/Player.ts`): single `_equippedWeapon: WeaponId` slot, `equipWeapon()`, `resetWeapon()`, `tryFire()` fires one weapon.
- `weapons.ts` (`src/utils/weapons.ts`): weapon catalogue with definitions for cannon, spread, dual, rapid — all persistent, no timeout model.
- `GymWeapons.ts` (`src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts`): `_collectDrop()` calls `player.equipWeapon()` or `player.resetWeapon()` — single-slot model.
- Weapon power-up drops: Spread, Dual, Rapid, Reset — round-robin, 7-second lifetime on screen.

## Desired change

1. **Player entity — weapon collection:** Replace `_equippedWeapon: WeaponId` with a weapon collection (e.g., a `Set<WeaponId>` for permanent weapons and a `Map<WeaponId, number>` for timed weapons tracking expiry timestamps). Update `equipWeapon()` to **add** to the collection, `resetWeapon()` to clear timed weapons.
2. **Player entity — auto-fire all weapons:** Update `tryFire()` to fire from **every active weapon** in the collection. Each weapon maintains its own cooldown. Emit bullets for all weapons whose cooldowns have elapsed this frame.
3. **Weapon timeout tracking:** Add per-weapon countdown logic. When a timed weapon's 10-second timer expires, remove it from the active set. Expose a method to tick and cull expired weapons.
4. **GymWeapons scene — updated collection:** Update `_collectDrop()` to call the new cumulative `equipWeapon()` (add, not replace). Reset clears timed weapons. No changes to the drop spawner itself.
5. **Constants:** Add a tunable `WEAPON_TIMEOUT_MS = 10000` constant (10 seconds) to `core/constants.ts`.
6. **Tests and documentation.**

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/entities/Player.ts` — major refactor: weapon collection with timers, multi-weapon auto-fire
- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — add timeout tracking helpers, possibly a `WeaponInstance` type with expiry
- `src/core/constants.ts` — add `WEAPON_TIMEOUT_MS = 10000`
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` — update collection logic for cumulative model
- `src/entities/Player.test.ts` — new tests for cumulative weapon behavior
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.test.ts` — update tests for cumulative model

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — breaking GymWeapons tests:** The existing scene tests assert single-weapon behavior. They will need updates. Mitigated: tests are well-structured and the changes are contained to Player + GymWeapons.
- **Risk — auto-fire complexity with multiple weapons:** Each weapon has its own cooldown; the firing logic must track cooldowns per-weapon. Mitigated: straightforward extension of the existing cooldown pattern.
- **Risk — visual clutter from multi-weapon bullets:** With 3-4 weapons firing simultaneously, the screen may be visually busy. Mitigated: bullets have distinct colors per weapon (existing palette supports this).
- **Scope-creep risk:** HUD display for active weapons and remaining timers is **out of scope** — this is a gameplay mechanic change, not a UI change.

## Related work

- **AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR** — "Weapon power-ups (3 patterns + reset) with auto-fire and weapon gym scene" (completed): the item that implemented the current persistent single-slot weapon system. This item **refactors** that system.
- **AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT** — "Create gym scene for power-ups with spawning, collection, and standalone HUD" (completed): generic power-up infrastructure.

## Plan: changelog

- **2026-09-14** — Plan auto-complete (pre-check: Extra Small effort, Low risk). Six automated review stages passed; AC coverage 100%. Appendix resolved (see below).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Weapon stacking model — when collecting Spread while having cannon, does the ship fire BOTH patterns simultaneously (cannon + spread), and if then collecting Dual, does it fire ALL three (cannon + spread + dual)?" — **Answer: Yes — cumulative (AC1: collecting adds to active set, no replacement; cannon always present)**. Final: cumulative, all fire simultaneously.
- Q2: "Timeout granularity — does each weapon power-up get its own independent 10-second timer (e.g., Spread collected at t=0 expires at t=10, Dual collected at t=5 expires at t=15), or does picking up any weapon reset ALL active weapon timers to 10 seconds?" — **Answer: Independent per-weapon timers (AC2: each weapon power-up gets its own independent 10-second countdown from the moment of collection)**. Final: independent countdowns.
- Q3: "Reset power-up behavior — with cumulative weapons, does Reset clear ALL timed weapons leaving only cannon, or does it work differently?" — **Answer: Clear all timed weapons, leaving only cannon (AC4: collecting the Reset power-up removes all timed weapons from the active set, leaving only the permanent cannon)**. Final: clears all timed weapons.
- Q4: "Any visual/audio feedback on weapon expiration? Or do timed weapons simply stop firing when their timer expires?" — **Answer: No special feedback — weapons simply stop firing (AC5: expired weapons are silently dropped)**. Final: silent expiration.

> All questions resolved by acceptance criteria encoding. No producer response needed.

# Intake Brief — One Tank changes colour (AH-0MTVYBL2L0085G6G)

## Problem statement

In the Tanks gym scene (`GymEnemies` booted with `enemyKey: 'tank'` from the gym index), one Tank — always the first alive in row-major spawn order (top-left initially) — renders green at rest and snaps to orange while any player thruster key is held, reverting to green on release. This color change communicates nothing to the player and should not happen: every Tank should render the Tank body colour at all times, independent of player input.

## Users

- **Player / playtester** — sees a stable, readable formation where colour identifies enemy type (orange = Tank); a Tank that flickers green↔orange with thrust input is confusing and looks broken.
- **Developer** — needs enemy body colour to be owned solely by entity construction/config, with no per-frame coupling to player input state.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, when I open the Tanks gym I see six orange Tanks; holding or releasing thrust never changes any Tank's colour, so I trust that colour means enemy type.
- As a **player**, when I destroy the discoloured top-left Tank, the next Tank does not inherit the wrong colour — every survivor stays Tank-orange.
- As a **developer**, I can assert in a headless test that Tank body colour is invariant across thrust-input frames and across destruction order.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Stable Tank colour:** booting the Tanks gym shows all alive Tanks in the Tank body colour at rest; holding any thrust key (arrows or WASD, either control scheme) changes no enemy's rendered colour; releasing changes nothing.
- [ ] **AC2 — No first-alive special-casing:** destroying Tanks in any order (top-left first, then left-to-right along rows, or any other order) never produces a wrong-coloured survivor; the "moves to the next alive" behaviour is gone.
- [ ] **AC3 — Regression test:** a headless test boots `GymEnemies` with the tank seed, simulates thrust-input frames, asserts every alive entity keeps the expected body colour, destroys the first entity and repeats for the next alive one. Fails before the fix, passes after.
- [ ] **AC4 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
- [ ] **AC5 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Engine/stack:** Phaser 4.2.1 + TypeScript, Vite, Vitest (existing stack).
- **No behaviour change beyond the colour fix:** hit/invulnerability/respawn logic, destruction audio ownership, formation drift, radial bursts, and the editor panel's live-apply semantics stay as they are.
- **Colour ownership:** entity body colour stays constructor/config-owned; the fix must remove the coupling, not paper over it with a per-frame repaint.
- **Scene lifecycle:** the fix must survive `GymEnemies` stop→restart reuse of the same scene instance (existing SHUTDOWN teardown pattern in `GymFormationScene`).

## Existing state

- There is no standalone `GymTank` scene anymore: the index "Tanks" entry routes to the shared `GymEnemies` scene with `{ enemyKey: 'tank' }` (`src/scenes/GymIndex.ts`, `src/utils/enemyGymDiscovery.ts`).
- Tank seed config is 6 tanks, `rect` formation, body colour `0xff6600` (`src/core/enemyConfig.ts` `DEFAULT_ENEMY_CONFIGS.tank`); entities are built via `createEnemyFromConfig` (`src/entities/enemyFactory.ts`), which passes `config.color` into the `Tank` constructor.
- `Tank._color` is `private readonly`, set only in the constructor, and `_drawBody()` runs only at construction (`src/entities/Tank.ts`). No `setTint`/`clearTint` calls exist anywhere in `src/`; no first-alive highlight code was found.
- Spawn order is row-major (`buildRectFormationOffsets`, 3 columns in `src/utils/formations.ts`), and `entities` array order is stable — consistent with the observed "top-left first, then next alive left-to-right" progression.
- The only runtime mutation of entity colour fields is `GymEnemies._applyLive()`, which writes `_color`/`_colorNumber`/`_size`/bullet tunings on **panel DOM input events only** — not on thrust input. Tank exposes all of those fields, so it is affected by panel edits like every other enemy.
- Player thruster flames use `thrustFlameColor 0xff8c00` / inner `0xffff00` (`src/core/config.ts`); the ship redraws its own `Graphics` per frame while flames animate (`Player.preUpdate` → `_redraw`). No code path was found linking player input state to any enemy's body graphics.
- `loadEnemyConfig()` merges any stored localStorage entry over the seed defaults — a stale stored tank config (e.g. a scout-green `0x00ff00` colour saved under the tank key) would persist silently across sessions.
- Panel DOM button colours (green `#2ecc71` Respawn, orange `#ff8c00` Save As, `src/style.css`) are plain-DOM and cannot repaint canvas Tank bodies; ruled out as the cause.

## Desired change

1. Reproduce headlessly and/or visually: boot `GymEnemies` with the tank seed, hold thrust, observe which entity (if any) reports/renders a non-Tank colour; confirm actual vs expected hex values.
2. Identify the root cause among the leading hypotheses (stale localStorage tank colour merged over seed defaults; per-frame graphics coupling between the player ship redraw and the first entity's body graphics; panel live-apply writing a wrong colour; other — investigate, do not assume).
3. Fix the root cause so Tank body colour is invariant across thrust input and destruction order; if a stale stored config is the cause, handle migration/invalidation so existing players recover without manual localStorage edits.
4. Add the AC3 regression test; keep the full suite green.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.ts` — Tanks scene (editor panel, `_applyLive`, `_onRespawn`, `collectBullets` tank branch `tryFireRadialBurst`).
- `src/entities/enemyFactory.ts` — `createEnemyFromConfig` builds the Tank with `config.color`.
- `src/core/enemyConfig.ts` — tank seed (`color: 0xff6600`) + `loadEnemyConfig` localStorage merge (staleness hypothesis).
- `src/entities/Tank.ts` — `_color` readonly, `_drawBody` at construction only; no repaint path today.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — thruster flame colours + per-frame `_redraw` (thrust-coupling hypothesis).
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — `tick()` loop, `setAimTarget`, entity ordering, `_handleCollisions`, SHUTDOWN teardown.
- `src/utils/formations.ts` — `buildRectFormationOffsets` row-major spawn order.
- `src/scenes/GymIndex.ts`, `src/utils/enemyGymDiscovery.ts` — "Tanks" index entry routing.
- `src/core/config.ts`, `src/core/constants.ts` — ship/flame colours (`0xff8c00`, `0x00ffff`, `0x00ff00` references for comparison).

**Key Files:**
- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.ts` — Scene under test; panel live-apply writes entity colour fields on DOM input.
- `src/entities/enemyFactory.ts` — Builds Tank from config colour; verify the value reaching the constructor.
- `src/core/enemyConfig.ts` — Seed defaults + localStorage merge; check for stale stored tank colour.
- `src/entities/Tank.ts` — Body rendering; needs invariant-colour regression coverage.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — Thruster input/flame path; rule out or confirm per-frame coupling.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — Tick/collision ordering behind the first-alive progression.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — root cause unconfirmed:** no code path found yet explains the symptom; the leading hypotheses (stale localStorage colour, per-frame graphics coupling) may both be wrong. Mitigation: AC3 forces a reproducer first; if headless repro fails, reproduce visually in-browser before fixing.
- **Risk — overlap with in-flight VFX work:** `AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V` (explosion VFX) touches the same per-entity colour area. Mitigation: coordinate merge order; keep this fix minimal and colour-ownership scoped.
- **Assumption — operator's colour report is literal:** "green" = `0x00ff00`, "orange" = `0xff6600`; implementer to verify actual rendered/stored hexes during repro.
- **Scope-creep guard:** editor-panel colour UX, per-enemy colour customization, and explosion-VFX tuning are out of scope; file as linked work items if desired.

## Related work

- `Add particle-based explosion VFX for enemy and player deaths (AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V)` — in-progress feature that tints explosion particles by entity base colour; touches the same colour-per-entity area, coordinate to avoid conflicts.
- `Player-enemy collision (AH-0MTV7JOLU006W8PT)` — has an uncommitted diff in its worktree touching `GymFormationScene._handleCollisions`; adjacent code, watch for overlap.
- `Rewrite GymTank gym scene on the core library (AH-0MTAN4T0I004H187)` — completed; history of the Tanks scene.
- `Create E3 Tank gym scene (AH-0MT99I2OC0014MNZ)` — completed; original scene.
- `Entity-centred explosion colour jitter (AH-0MTVID3I1001Y034)` — blocked; per-entity colour derivation.
- `Explosion particle test suite (AH-0MTVH6DQO0016CGJ)` — open; colour-centred assertions may overlap AC3.
- `Config-aware entity seam (AH-0MTF3FJL009T2QL)` — completed; the `_color`/`_size` live-patch seam used by `_applyLive`.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Which tank? Is it always the same tank (e.g., always position 0,0 or a specific slot), or does it vary?" — Answer (operator, 2026-09-11): "It starts with the one in the top left. If that is destroyed it moves to the next on the top row, then the next. If not top row left it changes to the bottom row and moves left to right as enemies are destroyed." Research: matches row-major spawn order (`buildRectFormationOffsets`, 3 cols) + stable `entities` array order; i.e. the first alive entity in spawn order.
- Q2: "What color does it change to? (e.g. thruster flame 0xff8c00, ship 0x00ffff?)" — Answer (operator, 2026-09-11): "green until thruster pressed then orange, then back to green when released." Research: green matches Scout-green `0x00ff00`, orange matches Tank-orange `0xff6600`; exact on-screen hexes unverified — implementer to confirm.
- Q3: "Timing — immediately on thrust, or delayed?" — Answer (operator, 2026-09-11): "immediately." Research: suggests a per-frame coupling rather than a timer/tween.
- Q4: "Which scene?" — Answer (operator, 2026-09-11): "Whatever scene is loaded when I click 'Tanks' from the index scene." Research: that is `GymEnemies` with `{ enemyKey: 'tank' }` (`GymIndex.ts` + `enemyGymDiscovery.ts`); no standalone `GymTank` exists.
- Q5: "Reproduction steps / screenshot?" — Answer (operator, 2026-09-11): "Load index, click Tanks, top left enemy is green, press thruster key (any) changes to orange, let go goes back to green, shoot it and the one to its right turns green and does the same." No screenshot provided. This is the AC1/AC2 repro.

## Related work (automated report)

*Populated by `/skill:find-related` at intake close (keywords: tank, colour, gym, thrusters, scene; repo matches: `README.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md`):*

- **Add player to each Enemy Gym scene (AH-0MTD0Z0Y7003T1NT)** — completed; put the keyboard-controlled Player ship into the Tanks scene, which is the precondition for the thrust/colour coupling reported here.
- **Validate full test suite and documentation consistency (AH-0MTBDB3240043TLA)** — completed; routine validation, no direct link.
- **Add ship deceleration when no inputs, with slider to control deceleration rate (AH-0MTAFH1ZF003EGDF)** — completed; player thrust/movement tuning, adjacent at most.

# Diver dive SFX (AH-0MTVYC6E8005YN6F)

**Headline:** Add two distinct procedural dive-phase sounds to the E2 Diver — a short "dive-start" cue played once at the FORMATION→DIVING transition, and a ~2-second continuous "dive whoosh" sustained for the dive duration — both wired entity-side in `Diver.ts` following the established `effects.ts` pattern.

## Problem statement

The E2 Diver entity (`src/entities/Diver.ts`) now has fire and destruction audio (AH-0MTCO1LGD0082SVG) but is silent on its signature behaviour: breaking formation and diving toward the player. The player gets no audible warning that a diver has begun its dive, and no sustained cue while the dive is in flight. Following GDD §7.3 enemy-audio feedback, add a distinct dive-start cue and a continuous dive sound, both distinguishable from the existing Diver fire (`playDiverFireSound`) and destruction (`playDiverDestructionSound`) sounds.

## Users

- **Players** — need an audible tell when a diver breaks formation (danger cue) and a sustained cue while the dive is in flight so the threat is trackable without watching every formation slot.
- **AI agents / developers** — need the sounds to follow the established procedural-audio pattern (`src/audio/effects.ts`) and degrade to safe no-ops in headless tests.

### Example user stories

- As a player, I want to hear a distinct cue the instant a diver breaks formation so I can react to the incoming dive.
- As a player, I want a sustained sound while the diver is diving so I can track the threat even when watching other enemies.
- As a developer, I want both sounds implemented via the existing `effects.ts` helpers so they degrade to safe no-ops in headless tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Dive-start cue** — A new `playDiverDiveStartSound()` exists in `src/audio/effects.ts`, played exactly **once per dive** at the FORMATION→DIVING transition (in `_startDive()`), distinct from the Diver fire and destruction sounds and from other enemies' cues.
- **Continuous dive sound** — A new sustained dive sound (start/stop pair or single ~2 s envelope matching `DIVER_DIVE_DURATION`) exists in `src/audio/effects.ts`, started at dive start and stopped when the dive ends (transition to RETURNING), so it plays for the whole dive and never leaks past it.
- **No leak on destruction/restart** — If the diver is destroyed mid-dive or the scene restarts mid-dive, the sustained dive sound stops (no orphaned oscillators). `destroySelf()` / `destroy()` and the SHUTDOWN teardown path must silence it.
- **Distinct character** — The two new sounds are distinct from each other AND from `playDiverFireSound()` / `playDiverDestructionSound()` (e.g. a rising whoosh/crack for dive-start, a sustained filtered-noise/sweep texture for the dive itself).
- **Safe degradation** — All new audio calls are safe no-ops without a working `AudioContext` (headless tests, browsers without Web Audio), preserving the `effects.ts` contract.
- **Tests** — New tests assert: dive-start cue fires exactly once per dive; the continuous sound starts at dive start and stops at dive end; no leak when destroyed mid-dive; degradation to no-op headless.
- **Documentation** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README (if it lists per-enemy audio), and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Procedural Web Audio only — no audio assets (existing `effects.ts` pattern).
- Follow enemy core-library best practices (`docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`).
- The continuous dive sound must have a bounded lifetime tied to the dive state machine (`DIVER_DIVE_DURATION = 2` s); it must not leak oscillators on destruction or scene restart (cf. `updateThrusterSound`/`stopThrusterSound` pattern for the player hum, and the SHUTDOWN teardown in AH-0MTPLHLZ3006MOC4).
- Multiple divers may dive concurrently — the dive-sound implementation must tolerate overlapping instances (per-dive nodes or a refcounted shared texture, implementer's choice, documented).
- Audio functions must degrade to safe no-ops in headless environments.
- Do not include CI/CD pipeline tests.

## Existing state

- `src/entities/Diver.ts` — state machine `FORMATION → DIVING → RETURNING`; `_startDive()` transitions at the end of the hold timer (`DIVER_HOLD_FORMATION_SECONDS = 3`); `_handleDive()` advances `_divePhase` over `DIVER_DIVE_DURATION = 2` s then moves to RETURNING. Has `playDiverFireSound()` (once per spread burst) and `playDestructionAudio()` → `playDiverDestructionSound()`; **no dive-phase sounds exist**.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — has `playDiverFireSound()` (~280→120 Hz sawtooth crack, 80 ms) and `playDiverDestructionSound()` (280→40 Hz + sine undertone, 0.35 s); has the player thruster-hum start/stop/update sustained-sound pattern (`updateThrusterSound`/`stopThrusterSound`) as the precedent for a continuous sound; **no Diver dive sounds exist**.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — drives divers via `entity.applyFormationPosition(...)` in `tick()`; per-frame entity updates make an entity-side start/stop call site natural (no scene change expected).
- Reference: AH-0MTCO1LGD0082SVG ("Diver has no audio") — completed; added the fire + destruction sounds this item builds on.

## Desired change

- **New sounds**: add `playDiverDiveStartSound()` (short distinct cue, e.g. rising whoosh/crack) and a sustained dive-sound start/stop pair (e.g. filtered-noise/sweep texture, ~2 s, matching the dive duration) to `src/audio/effects.ts`, all safe no-ops without an `AudioContext`.
- **Diver entity**: call the dive-start cue exactly once in `_startDive()`; start the sustained sound on dive start and stop it when the dive ends (DIVING→RETURNING transition), in `destroySelf()`/`destroy()`, and anywhere the entity can be torn down mid-dive (null-scene guard precedent applies).

**Key Files:**

- `src/audio/effects.ts` — add `playDiverDiveStartSound()` + sustained dive-sound start/stop (procedural Web Audio, safe no-op guard; overlap-safe for concurrent divers).
- `src/entities/Diver.ts` — call dive-start cue once in `_startDive()`; start/stop the sustained sound with the DIVING state; silence it in `destroySelf()`/`destroy()`.
- `src/entities/Diver.test.ts` — dive-start once-per-dive test; sustained start/stop lifecycle test; no-leak-on-destroy test; headless no-op test.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — update the `GymDiver` audio row / audio section to mention the dive-phase sounds (if it lists per-enemy audio).
- `README.md` — update the `src/audio/effects.ts` bullet to mention the dive sounds (if per-enemy).

## Related work

- **Diver has no audio (AH-0MTCO1LGD0082SVG)** — completed; added Diver fire + destruction sounds. This item's sounds must be distinct from those.
- **Scout has no audio (AH-0MTCO1LDA008RA19)** — completed; sibling fire-sound + advance-cue item.
- **Swarm has no audio (AH-0MTCO1L74003CAQJ)** — completed; sibling burst-sound item.
- **Stale formation entities crash on GymEnemies scene restart (AH-0MTPLHLZ3006MOC4)** — completed; SHUTDOWN teardown precedent — relevant to the no-leak-on-restart requirement.
- **Player thruster hum (AH-0MTFOSOHN001Q620)** — completed; `updateThrusterSound`/`stopThrusterSound` sustained-sound precedent.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Continuous-sound lifecycle (medium)**: a sustained sound tied to a state machine can leak oscillators if the diver is destroyed or the scene restarts mid-dive. Mitigation: stop calls in `destroySelf()`/`destroy()` + SHUTDOWN teardown coverage; a no-leak test is an AC.
- **Concurrent divers (low)**: several divers may dive at once; overlapping sustained sounds must not corrupt shared module state. Mitigation: per-dive nodes or documented refcounting; implementer chooses and documents.
- **Distinctness is subjective**: "distinct" is judged by ear (different oscillator type / frequency range / envelope from fire + destruction). Mitigation: document the chosen character in code comments; reviewers listen in-browser.
- **Assumption**: entity-side wiring (no base-scene seam needed) — the dive lifecycle is fully inside `Diver.ts`, unlike destruction audio which the base scene owns. If the implementer finds a scene seam is needed, that is a small adjustment.
- **Scope creep**: no changes to fire/destruction sounds, no advance warning before the dive (producer: cue plays AT the transition), no other enemies' audio.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1**: Should the preparation sound play at the exact FORMATION→DIVING transition, or as an advance warning (≥ 500 ms lead)? — **Answer (producer): "at transition"** — the cue plays at the moment the Diver transitions (in `_startDive()`), not before. Source: interactive reply 2026-09-11.
- **Q2**: Should the dive sound be continuous through the ~2 s dive, or a short burst at dive start? — **Answer (producer): "continuous"** — a sustained sound for the whole dive duration, stopped when the dive ends. Source: interactive reply 2026-09-11.
- **Q3**: Should the two sounds be distinct from each other and from the existing Diver fire/destruction sounds? — **Answer (producer): "distinct"** — both new sounds are distinct from each other and from the existing palette. Source: interactive reply 2026-09-11.

**Research summary**: Inspected `src/entities/Diver.ts` (FORMATION→DIVING→RETURNING state machine; `_startDive()` transition point; `DIVER_DIVE_DURATION = 2` s; existing fire/destruction wiring, no dive-phase sounds), `src/audio/effects.ts` (existing `playDiverFireSound`/`playDiverDestructionSound`; player `updateThrusterSound`/`stopThrusterSound` sustained-sound precedent with no-op degradation), `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` (entity driven per-frame via `applyFormationPosition` in `tick()` — entity-side wiring is natural, no scene seam expected), and the completed AH-0MTCO1LGD0082SVG item (fire + destruction sounds this item builds on).

# Tighten Enemy Hit Radii to Match Visual Size

## Problem statement

Enemy hitboxes use a flat 20px radius regardless of visual size, making small enemies (Scout: 16px, Phaser: 14px, Swarm: 15px) have hitboxes 2.5–3× larger than their visuals. This causes hits to feel imprecise — bullets destroy enemies without visibly overlapping them, and the player can be "killed" by flying past an enemy without visually colliding.

## Users

- **Player**: Needs intuitive hit feedback — when a bullet hits an enemy or the player crashes into one, the visual collision should be believable. Currently, bullets can destroy enemies from apparent distances of 10–12px away, and the player can be killed from similar apparent gaps.
- **Developer / tuning**: Needs a single globally configurable knob for the hit-radius buffer, adjustable without code changes to per-entity logic.

## Current State

| Entity | Visual Half-Size | Hit Radius | Ratio |
|--------|-----------------|------------|-------|
| Scout (E1) | 8px | 20px | 2.5× |
| Diver (E2) | 9px | 20px | 2.2× |
| Tank (E3) | 14px | 20px | 1.4× |
| Phaser (E4) | 7px | 20px | 2.9× |
| Swarm (E5) | 7.5px | 20px | 2.7× |
| Boss | ~50px | 20px | 0.4× |

- All enemies use `DEFAULT_ENTITY_HIT_RADIUS = 20` (px) from `GymFormationScene.ts`.
- Collision uses circle-vs-circle via `Math.hypot <= rA + rB`.
- `entityHitRadius` is configurable via `EnemyFormationConfig.entityHitRadius` but no scene sets it.
- The Boss uses the same 20px hit radius despite its 50px visual radius.
- Player hull is `SHIP_SIZE / 2 = 10px`.
- The collision check covers two directions: (a) player bullets vs enemy bodies, and (b) enemy bullets vs player body and player body vs enemy bodies.

## Proposed Change

Add a `getHitRadius()` method to each enemy entity that returns a hit radius proportional to its visual size, with a configurable gameplay buffer:

```
hitRadius = ceil(visualHalfSize + HIT_RADIUS_BUFFER_PX)
```

Where `HIT_RADIUS_BUFFER_PX` is a global constant (default: 2px) covering visual stroke thickness and small visual uncertainty.

| Entity | Visual Half-Size | Proposed Hit Radius (buffer=2) |
|--------|-----------------|-------------------------------|
| Scout (E1) | 8px | 10px |
| Diver (E2) | 9px | 11px |
| Tank (E3) | 14px | 16px |
| Phaser (E4) | 7px | 9px |
| Swarm (E5) | 7.5px | 10px |
| Boss | ~50px | 52px |

- Each entity implements `getHitRadius()` returning its configured hit radius.
- `GymFormationScene._handleCollisions()` calls `entity.getHitRadius()` instead of the flat default.
- The collision check covers both: (a) player bullets vs enemy bodies, and (b) player body vs enemy bodies.
- `HIT_RADIUS_BUFFER_PX` is declared in `src/core/constants.ts` and used by both entities and the scene.
- The `entityHitRadius` config option remains as an override mechanism (for gym tuning).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Player-bullet hit precision**: A player bullet must visibly overlap an enemy to destroy it. Hit radii are proportional to visual size (verified via unit tests checking `entity.getHitRadius()` returns expected values for Scout, Diver, Tank, Phaser, Swarm, Boss).
2. **Player-body hit precision**: Flying into an enemy body only registers a hit when the player hull visually overlaps the enemy. Uses `entity.getHitRadius()` (buffer baked in) for the enemy radius and `SHIP_SIZE / 2` for the player radius.
3. **Configurable buffer**: `HIT_RADIUS_BUFFER_PX` is a global constant in `src/core/constants.ts` (default: 2px). Changing it adjusts all hit radii proportionally.
4. **Boss hit radius scales to visual size**: The Boss uses a hit radius proportional to its visual size (≥ 48px, matching its ~50px visual radius with buffer).
5. **Player-bullet vs enemy collision uses entity's hit radius**: `GymFormationScene._handleCollisions()` calls `entity.getHitRadius()` for the enemy radius in the player-bullet collision check.
6. **Player-vs-enemy-body collision uses entity's hit radius**: The player-vs-enemy-body collision check (step 4) calls `entity.getHitRadius()` for the enemy radius and `SHIP_SIZE / 2` for the player radius (the buffer is already baked into `getHitRadius()`).
7. **Enemy-vs-enemy collision unaffected**: Enemies still pass through each other freely (GDD §2.6).
8. **Backward compatibility**: The `entityHitRadius` config option on `EnemyFormationConfig` still works as an override for gym scenes.
9. **Testing**: Unit tests verify hit radius values per entity type and collision behavior with tight hitboxes (both player-bullet and player-body paths).
10. **Documentation**: Entity classes document their hit radius logic in comments.
11. **Test suite passes**: All existing tests pass with the new hit radii.

## Constraints

- Must remain circle-vs-circle (no pixel-perfect or rectangle collision) — this is a radius adjustment, not a detection algorithm change.
- Performance impact: negligible (same O(n×m) collision checks, just different radii).
- No changes to enemy bullet hit radius (`DEFAULT_BULLET_HIT_RADIUS = 6px`).
- `HIT_RADIUS_BUFFER_PX` default of 2px provides a minimal gameplay buffer for visual stroke thickness; should not be confused with the old 20px flat radius.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/constants.ts` — add `HIT_RADIUS_BUFFER_PX` global constant
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — `_handleCollisions()` to call `entity.getHitRadius()` for both player-bullet and player-body collision paths
- `src/entities/Scout.ts` — add `getHitRadius()` returning visual half-size + buffer
- `src/entities/Diver.ts` — add `getHitRadius()` returning visual half-size + buffer
- `src/entities/Tank.ts` — add `getHitRadius()` returning visual half-size + buffer
- `src/entities/Phaser.ts` — add `getHitRadius()` returning visual half-size + buffer
- `src/entities/Swarm.ts` — add `getHitRadius()` returning visual half-size + buffer
- `src/entities/Boss.ts` — add `getHitRadius()` returning visual half-size + buffer

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep risk** — Pixel-perfect (per-pixel alpha) collision is explicitly out of scope; this is a proportional-radius adjustment. Record pixel-perfect detection as a separate linked work item if requested later.
- **Difficulty shift** — Smaller enemy hitboxes make enemies harder to hit; this matches the operator's intent ("only hit when there is an actual collision") but is a deliberate gameplay change.
- **Assumption** — `HIT_RADIUS_BUFFER_PX = 2` covers visual stroke thickness; tuning is a constant change, not a code change.
- **Test regression risk** — Existing tests may assert the old 20px-radius hit behavior; verify and update collision tests as needed.
- **Assumption** — The 10% margin in the original draft is replaced by the flat `HIT_RADIUS_BUFFER_PX` buffer per operator direction (globally configurable).
- **Player hull unchanged** — Player hit radius stays `SHIP_SIZE / 2`; only enemy radii change.

## Related Work

- **AH-0MTECNG8W00403EH** — Implement: Core scene — collision detection and player hit/respawn (parent work, completed)
- **AH-0MTECNG4K0071TIB** — Test: Core scene — collision detection and player hit/respawn (related tests, completed)
- **AH-0MTV7JOLU006W8PT** — If player crashes into an enemy, they both die (player-vs-enemy collision, completed)

### Related work (automated report)

#### Related work items
- **AH-0MT99K3FE008CT13** — Create E4 Phaser gym scene (completed)
- **AH-0MTC2P6G3007PJ40** — Create combat gym scene for combat-coupled power-ups (P3 Shield, P4 Bomb, P6 Phase Shift, P7 Teleport) with low-level enemy threats (completed)
- **AH-0MT994ESD000RP1Q** — Create E1 Scout gym scene (completed)

#### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: actual, collision, enemies, hit, hits (+6 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: actual, collision, enemies, hit, hits (+6 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: collision, enemies, hit, hits, player (+5 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Intake session 2026-09-12 (agent Map). Prior intake session (2026-09-12T01:50) left three open questions; they were answered in this session's interactive review.

- Q: "The description says 'hits are not pixel perfect' — can you clarify what approach is preferred? 1. Pixel-perfect collision, 2. Tighter bounding shapes, 3. Proportional hit radius?" (comment AH-C0MTXQ9RO9009W4TK)
  — Answer (operator, interactive reply): **Proportional hit radius** (option 3), with the gameplay buffer made **globally configurable**. Pixel-perfect alpha collision is out of scope. Source: interactive reply this session.

- Q: "The description mentions '(and maybe the player)' — should the player ship also have tighter collision detection? Also, should enemy bullets vs enemy entity collision be affected, or only player bullets vs enemies?" (comment AH-C0MTXQ9ZG20004O4T)
  — Answer (operator, interactive reply): "This should be player bullets and player body." Both player-bullet-vs-enemy and player-body-vs-enemy collision paths use the tightened enemy hit radius. Source: interactive reply this session.

- Q: "The Boss entity (GDD §4.3) uses a 50px visual radius but currently gets a 20px hit radius from the default. Should the Boss also get tighter collision matching?" (comment AH-C0MTXQA6CN005C8V0)
  — Status: **not explicitly answered**. The finalized draft includes the Boss with a visual-proportional radius (≈52px) for consistency; the operator raised no objection to this inclusion during draft review. Treated as an accepted assumption (documented in Risks & assumptions) — the operator may override at review.

- Q: "How large should the gameplay buffer be?" (derived from this session's direction to make it globally configurable)
  — Answer (agent proposal accepted by non-objection): default `HIT_RADIUS_BUFFER_PX = 2` px, declared in `src/core/constants.ts`, applied uniformly to every entity. Changing the constant rescales all hit radii. Source: agent-derived; operator directed global configurability without specifying a value.

### Prior answers changed

- Original draft proposed a 10% proportional margin (`ceil(visualHalfSize × 1.1)`). Final accepted approach replaces it with a flat, globally configurable `HIT_RADIUS_BUFFER_PX = 2` px additive buffer, per operator direction ("Make the gameplay buffer globally configurable").

# Create a playable game

## Problem statement

The project has a fully populated set of gym scenes (enemy, boss, power-up, combat, weapons, player), entity classes (Player, Scout, Diver, Tank, Phaser, Swarm, Boss), power-up system (P3–P9), HUD, SFX, and the `GymFormationScene` core library — but no playable game. The `gameConfig.ts` registers only `GymIndex` (a dev-mode gym selector) as the boot scene. We need a complete game loop: a main menu, a playable game scene with progressive wave/level management (5 levels + 1 boss), game-over flow with scoring and leaderboard integration, and proper scene navigation.

## Users

- **Playtester**: As a playtester, I want to boot the game into a menu, select Play Game, and experience 5 progressively difficult levels followed by a final boss encounter, with lives, score tracking, and a game-over screen — all in the Tron-inspired neon aesthetic.
- **Developer**: As a developer, I want the playable game to compose existing gym-scene components (enemy spawning, boss phases, power-up drops, collision detection, HUD) into a coherent level structure without duplicating logic.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Main Menu** — A `MenuScene` is the boot scene (replacing the current `GymIndex`-only config); it offers a **Play Game** button that starts Level 1 and a **Gym Scene Index** button that navigates to the existing `GymIndex` dev scene. The menu uses neon-cyan UI text on a dark background consistent with the GDD colour palette (§7.1).
2. **Playable game scene with wave/level management** — A new `PlayScene` (or similar) manages the 5-level progression: Levels 1–3 feature formation-based enemies with no enemy fire (GDD §3.2, §2.4); Level 4 introduces enemy-fired bullets; Level 5 has fewer enemies with predictable bullet patterns. Beating all enemies in a level advances to the next level automatically.
3. **Boss encounter** — The final boss (Central AI) appears after Level 5, using the existing 4-phase health bar and attack patterns from `Boss.ts`. The boss spawns minion enemies as a phase mechanic (matching the description's intent, GDD §4.3).
4. **Lives, scoring, game-over flow** — The player starts with 3 lives (up to 5 with P8 Extra Life); a hit costs one life. Score increases on enemy/boss destruction per GDD §4.5 (enemy point values, time bonus). When lives reach zero, the game-over screen displays the final score, prompts for a 3-character initials entry, and saves to the leaderboard work item (AH-0MU6VSKZT006HBTR).
5. **Navigation** — Game over returns to the main menu. The Gym Scene Index remains reachable via a button on the main menu (dev-only access, not hidden but clearly marked as a dev tool).
6. **HUD** — The existing `HUD.ts` (lives counter, active effects) is displayed during gameplay. Score is shown in the top-right corner in neon style.
7. **Scene navigation** — Proper Phaser scene transitions: Menu → PlayScene → GameOverScene → Menu. No scene leaks or orphaned references.
8. **Tests and full suite** — New automated unit/scene tests cover wave/level management, boss minion spawning, scoring/lives/game-over transitions, and scene wiring; existing gym-scene tests are not broken. The full project test suite (`npm test`) must pass with the new changes.
9. **Documentation** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Risks & assumptions

- **GymFormationScene API surface** — The `GymFormationScene` core library's internals (spawn logic, button handlers, HUD binding) are currently tuned for gym-scene interaction patterns (button-driven spawning). Reusing it for the playable game may require widening `protected`/`public` visibility or extracting a shared wave-manager interface.
- **Audio autoplay policy** (GDD §6.7) — Phaser's Web Audio context won't start before a user gesture. The menu's Play button must initialize audio; the game starts silently otherwise.
- **Scene memory management** — Switching between Menu → PlayScene → GameOverScene → Menu must properly destroy scene state (event listeners, timers, graphics) to avoid memory leaks or stale references.
- **GymEnemies vs. PlayScene** — `GymEnemies` is designed as a gym (button-driven, single-enemy, respawn loops). # Problem Statement

The Diver entity begins its return glide to formation the instant it reaches the dive target. This creates an unnaturally snappy behaviour — there is no momentary pause at the bottom of the arc, which breaks the intended "dive → hover → return" visual rhythm described in the GDD.

# Users

- **Player:** Expects enemy dive attacks to read as deliberate and telegraphed; a brief pause at the apex of the dive arc improves readability and fairness.
- **Developer:** Needs a clean, configurable pause that integrates into the existing state machine without breaking the drift-return or hold-loop logic.

# Acceptance Criteria

1. **PAUSING state introduced:** A new `DiverState.PAUSING` value exists and the diver enters it immediately after `_handleDive` completes (i.e. when `_divePhase >= 1`), *before* transitioning to `RETURNING`.
2. **Configurable pause duration:** A new constant `DIVER_PAUSE_DURATION` (default: 500 ms) controls how long the diver remains in `PAUSING`; the value is configurable via `DiverConfig` as an optional property.
3. **Behaviour during pause:** While in `PAUSING`, the diver holds its position at the dive target (no x/y movement), continues facing the player (`_updateFacingRotation` runs each frame), and does not fire spread shots (shoot mode is inactive during pause).
4. **Transition to RETURNING:** After the pause timer expires, the diver transitions to `DiverState.RETURNING` and begins its normal glide to the current formation slot. The hold timer resets to 0 so the next formation-hold cycle starts correctly.
5. **Tests:** Unit tests verify (a) the diver enters `PAUSING` state at dive completion, (b) the pause duration defaults to 500 ms, (c) a configurable duration overrides the default, (d) the diver transitions to `RETURNING` after the pause elapses, and (e) position is held during the pause.

# Constraints

- **Single-file change:** All changes live in `src/entities/Diver.ts` — no scene, audio, or VFX modifications.
- **Backward compatible:** Default behaviour matches the spec (500 ms pause); existing callers that do not pass `pauseDuration` are unaffected.
- **No state machine gaps:** The pause must be a distinct state — the diver cannot simply `sleep` in `DIVING` or `RETURNING`, because other systems (e.g. aim tracking, debug state inspection, future extensions) may query `behaviourState`.
- **Sound:** The sustained dive sound stops at the end of the dive (existing behaviour); no new audio is needed during the pause.

# Existing State

- `_handleDive()` completes, sets `_state = DiverState.RETURNING` and `_returnProgress = 0` — zero delay.
- `DiverState` enum has three values: `FORMATION`, `DIVING`, `RETURNING`.
- `DiverConfig` has no pause-related fields.
- The hold timer (`_holdTimer`) governs the formation-hold phase before the next dive; it is reset on entry to `DIVING` and again on entry to `RETURNING`.

# Desired Change

1. Add `PAUSING` to `DiverState` enum.
2. Add `DIVER_PAUSE_DURATION = 500` constant (ms).
3. Add optional `pauseDuration?: number` to `DiverConfig`.
4. Add `_pauseTimer = 0` field and `_pauseDuration` field to the class.
5. In `_handleDive()`, on dive completion: set `_state = PAUSING`, `_pauseTimer = 0`, stop dive sound (existing).
6. Add `_handlePause(dt)` method: advance `_pauseTimer`; if `>= _pauseDuration`, set `_state = RETURNING`, `_returnProgress = 0`, reset `_holdTimer`.
7. Wire `_handlePause` into `applyFormationPosition` switch.
8. In `_handlePause`, run `_updateFacingRotation(dt)` (diver still tracks player while paused).
9. Default `_pauseDuration` to `DIVER_PAUSE_DURATION`; allow `DiverConfig.pauseDuration` to override.
10. Write unit tests.

# Key Files (predicted)

- `src/entities/Diver.ts` — Add `PAUSING` state, pause duration constant/field, `_handlePause()`, wire into `applyFormationPosition`, add `pauseDuration` to `DiverConfig`.
- `src/entities/Diver.test.ts` — New tests for pause state entry, duration, configurable override, position hold, transition to RETURNING.

# Related Work

- **AH-0MTEI361E000IXYB** — Fix Diver.ts: lock x during dive and smooth return (completed; established the current `_handleReturn` drift-aware return logic this pause precedes).
- **AH-0MTEI0XRD0042ZEZ** — Write AC2+AC3: smooth return and no jump tests (completed; regression tests for the return path).
- **AH-0MTCP1CKB00480BD** — Diver jumps on return from dive (completed; the bug that motivated the return fix).
- **AH-0MTEHZNY9008O98Y** — Write AC1: no horizontal movement during dive test (completed).
- **AH-0MTECNI8K008FSKH** — Implement: Core scene — enemy live aim tracking (completed; `setAimTarget` seam the diver uses for player-facing rotation).

# Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: Should the pause occur (a) after the dive completes but before transitioning to RETURNING state, or (b) inside the RETURNING state? — Answer (operator): (a), after dive completes, before transitioning to RETURNING. Source: interactive reply.
- Q: Should we introduce a new PAUSING state, or keep the diver in its current state? — Answer (operator): Yes, new PAUSING state. Source: interactive reply.
- Q: Is 500ms definitive, or should it be configurable? — Answer (operator): Configurable via DiverConfig, default 500ms. Source: interactive reply.

# Swarm are too powerful when shooting (AH-0MU0F1T2H003B4K0)

## Problem statement

When shooting is enabled every member of the E5 Swarm formation (15 entities) fires on every 900 ms cycle, producing a near-unavoidable wall of bullets that makes the swarm disproportionately more powerful than every other enemy type. Add a per-entity `shotProbability` — the chance that an individual enemy fires on any given shot cycle — set to **25%** for the Swarm and **100%** for all other enemies.

## Users

- As a **player**, I want the swarm to feel threatening but survivable, so a large cluster of small enemies does not out-damage every other encounter.
- As a **designer**, I want per-enemy fire probability exposed in `EnemyConfig` and the gym editor panel, so I can tune enemy threat without editing code.

### Example user stories

- As a player, when I face the Swarm at Level 4+, I want only a fraction of the cluster to fire each volley so the bullet wall is manageable.
- As a designer, I want to open the enemy gym, drag a `shotProbability` slider for the Swarm, and immediately see the volley density change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Schema:** `EnemyConfig` (`src/core/enemyConfig.ts`) gains a required `shotProbability: number` field (fraction `0.0`–`1.0` per shot cycle). Every `DEFAULT_ENEMY_CONFIGS` seed entry supplies it: `swarm` = `0.25`; `scout`/`diver`/`tank`/`phaser`/`boss` = `1.0`. The generic fallback config in `loadEnemyConfig` also defaults to `1.0`.
- [ ] **AC2 — Entity gate:** Each enemy entity (`Scout`, `Diver`, `Tank`, `Phaser`, `Swarm`, `Boss`) accepts `shotProbability` through its existing config seam (default `1.0` when omitted, preserving current behaviour) and, when its fire interval elapses, only fires if a random draw succeeds. On a failed draw the cycle is consumed (interval timer resets) and no bullet is produced; the next cycle rolls again.
- [ ] **AC3 — Injectable randomness:** The probability roll per entity uses an injectable random source (defaults to `Math.random`) so tests can force fire/skip deterministically without statistical flakiness.
- [ ] **AC4 — Swarm reduction / no regression:** With `shotProbability = 0.25`, a forced-success roll makes a swarm member fire and a forced-failure roll makes it skip without emitting a bullet; the other enemies with `1.0` always fire when the interval elapses. Over a deterministic forced sequence the swarm emits ~1 bullet per 4 cycles per member.
- [ ] **AC5 — Factory threading:** `createEnemyFromConfig` (`src/entities/enemyFactory.ts`) threads `shotProbability` from the config into every entity constructor.
- [ ] **AC6 — Gym panel:** `GymEnemies` renders a `shotProbability` slider immediately after the `fireInterval` slider (fraction range, e.g. `0`–`1` step `0.05`), seeds it from the active config, live-applies it to spawned entities, and round-trips it through Save / Save As… (Save As default `1.0`).
- [ ] **AC7 — Testing/validation:** Automated tests cover the probability gate for each entity (forced success, forced failure, default `1.0`), `enemyConfig` load/save/merge defaults (including legacy persisted configs), factory threading, and the new gym panel slider. No test relies on `Math.random` alone.
- [ ] **AC8 — Documentation:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries. (Specifically: `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §8.1 field table, §8.4 entity seam, §8.5 editor-panel notes; `EnemyConfig` and entity JSDoc.)
- [ ] **AC9 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Additive only:** `shotProbability` defaults to `1.0`, so all current enemies behave exactly as before except the Swarm. Existing tests must stay green.
- **Tell interaction (Scout/Phaser):** these entities use a two-phase "tell" (advance audio cue → shot). The probability roll must be evaluated at the decision point (when the interval elapses / the tell starts), never after a tell has been scheduled, so a skipped cycle can never play a cue that produces no shot.
- **Diver dive behaviour:** Diver fires via `tryFireSpreadBurst` alongside its dive cycle; the gate must sit at the same interval check so a failed roll does not corrupt dive state.
- **Swarm volley semantics:** the coordinated volley is defined by multiple members returning bullets in the same frame; per-member rolls intentionally reduce volley density (average ~3–4 of 15 members per cycle at 25%).
- **Storage back-compat:** `loadEnemyConfig` merges saved JSON over seed defaults, so pre-existing saved configs (no `shotProbability`) inherit the seed value (Swarm `0.25`); custom keys with no seed use the generic fallback (`1.0`).
- **Units:** fraction `0.0`–`1.0` (matches `Math.random() < p`), not a 0–100 percentage.

## Existing state

- `EnemyConfig` and `DEFAULT_ENEMY_CONFIGS` live in `src/core/enemyConfig.ts`; the `swarm` seed has `fireInterval: 900`, `bulletSpeed: 180`, `count: 15`.
- Entities `src/entities/{Scout,Diver,Tank,Phaser,Swarm,Boss}.ts` each accept an optional seam config (`size? color? bulletColor? bulletSize? bulletSpeed? fireInterval? burstCount?`) and gate firing on `now - _lastFireTime < _fireInterval`.
- `createEnemyFromConfig` in `src/entities/enemyFactory.ts` builds an `opts` object from the config and dispatches to the entity class by key (unknown keys fall back to Scout).
- `GymEnemies` (`src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.ts`) derives its `EnemyFormationConfig` from `EnemyConfig`, dispatches `collectBullets` by key, and builds the DOM editor panel with slider ranges in `ENEMY_SLIDER_RANGES`.
- Docs: `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §8.1 (EnemyConfig table), §8.4 (entity seam), §8.5 (panel).

## Desired change

- Extend `EnemyConfig`/seeds/fallback and `createEnemyFromConfig` with `shotProbability` (fraction `0`–`1`).
- Each entity stores `_shotProbability` (default `1.0`) plus an injectable RNG; when the interval elapses, roll `rng() < _shotProbability`; on failure consume the cycle and return no bullet, on success continue the existing fire path.
- Add the `shotProbability` slider to the gym editor panel after `fireInterval`, wired into live-apply and Save / Save As.
- Extend unit tests and update the enemy-design documentation.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/enemyConfig.ts` — Add `shotProbability` to the interface, seed defaults (swarm `0.25`, others `1.0`) and the generic fallback (`1.0`).
- `src/entities/Scout.ts` — Probability gate at the tell decision point; injectable RNG; seam field.
- `src/entities/Diver.ts` — Probability gate in `tryFireSpreadBurst` at the interval check.
- `src/entities/Tank.ts` — Probability gate in `tryFireRadialBurst`.
- `src/entities/Phaser.ts` — Probability gate at the tell decision point.
- `src/entities/Swarm.ts` — Probability gate in `tryFireBurstBullet`; swarm seed `0.25`.
- `src/entities/Boss.ts` — Probability gate in its fire path (default `1.0`, no behaviour change).
- `src/entities/enemyFactory.ts` — Thread `shotProbability` into the entity `opts`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.ts` — Add `shotProbability` to `ENEMY_SLIDER_RANGES`, render the slider after `fireInterval`, live-apply patches `_shotProbability`.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — §8.1 field table, §8.4 seam, §8.5 panel notes.
- Tests: `src/core/enemyConfig.test.ts`, `src/entities/*.test.ts` (Scout/Diver/Tank/Phaser/Swarm/Boss), `src/entities/enemyFactory.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.test.ts`.

## Related work

- **Config-aware entity seam (AH-0MTHG51KB007F17K)** — completed — added the `fireInterval`/`burstCount` config seam this change extends; entities already expose `effectiveSize`/`effectiveColor` getters and `_*` seam fields.
- **EnemyConfig schema and localStorage persistence (AH-0MTHG51A6003EX9S)** — completed — the schema/persistence this adds a field to (`loadEnemyConfig` merge-over-defaults handles legacy entries).
- **Enemy Design tooling (AH-0MTFP7EIC004F1MN)** — completed — parent epic of the config/panel work; the gym panel this adds a control to.
- **Create E5 Swarm gym scene (AH-0MT99N53O0077KHC)** — completed — introduced the swarm entity/formation.
- **Gym scene sliders bound to live ship config (AH-0MTA8DMBH007MEHG)** — completed — established the slider/live-bind panel pattern mirrored here.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — tell/RNG interaction:** rolling for probability after a Scout/Phaser tell starts would play a cue with no shot. *Mitigation:* roll at the decision point; add a forced-skip test asserting no tell starts.
- **Risk — test flakiness from randomness.** *Mitigation:* injectable RNG; force success/failure rather than statistical assertions.
- **Risk — scope creep (rebalancing):** this item must only add the probability gate; do not re-tune other stats or redesign the coordinated volley. Extra opportunities are recorded as linked work items, not absorbed here.
- **Risk — persisted-config drift:** existing saved swarm configs without `shotProbability` inherit the seed (`0.25`); custom keys with no seed get `1.0`, so a custom swarm clone could stay over-powered. Documented and acceptable (custom enemies are user-owned; the panel exposes the control).
- **Risk — Diver dive coupling:** gating at the wrong point could leave the dive cycle out of sync. *Mitigation:* gate at the existing interval check and cover with a test.
- **Assumption:** units are a fraction `0.0`–`1.0`.
- **Assumption:** "all other enemies" includes `Boss` (default `1.0`; no behaviour change required for this item).
- **Assumption:** a failed roll consumes the cycle (no retry-until-success within the same cycle).
- **Assumption:** `shotProbability` is persisted in `localStorage` and surfaced in the gym panel, consistent with the other `EnemyConfig` fields.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q:** Confirm 25% per Swarm member reduces volley density (~3–4 of 15 fire per cycle). — **Answer:** Confirmed. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q:** Other enemies (Scout/Diver/Tank/Phaser) stay at 100% (no behaviour change). — **Answer:** Confirmed. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q:** Should `shotProbability` be persisted and visible in the gym panel? — **Answer:** Persisted and visible. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q:** Where should the panel control appear? — **Answer:** A new slider after `fireInterval`. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q:** Default value for custom (Save As…) enemies? — **Answer:** 100%. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q:** Field name in `EnemyConfig`? — **Answer:** `shotProbability`. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q:** Is Boss in scope for the field (default 100%)? — **Answer:** Yes. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q:** Injectable RNG for deterministic tests? — **Answer:** Injectable. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q:** Generic fallback config default for keys with no seed? — **Answer:** 100% (yes). Source: interactive reply.
- **Q:** Units — fraction 0.0–1.0 or percentage 0–100? — **Answer:** Fraction `0.0`–`1.0`. Source: interactive reply.

- **AH-0MTPLHLZ3006MOC4** – Stale formation entities crash on GymEnemies scene restart (Tank/Swarm/Diver/Phaser) (completed)

# Spawn power-ups in all combat gym scenes

## Headline

Add weighted-random, live-tunable power-up spawning (with random, enemy-avoiding placement and full collection) to the enemy-bearing combat gyms `GymEnemies` and `GymBoss`, backed by a new general game-rules config and the existing pluggable `PowerUpSpawner` interface.

## Original request (verbatim)

> We need to spawn power ups in all gym scenes. There should be a plugable spawner. The initial implementation will simply pick a power up at random from all those available and place it at a random place on the screen (not on top of enemies). The frequency of spawn will be a configuation in the main game config file (if no such file exists then create a config system).

## Problem statement

The enemy-bearing combat gyms — `GymEnemies` (every archetype) and `GymBoss` — spawn no power-ups at all, so a tester cannot observe drop cadence, placement or collection while under real enemy pressure. The three power-up/weapon gyms that do spawn drops use a hard-coded round-robin sequence at fixed screen positions with a compile-time interval (`POWER_UP_SPAWN_INTERVAL`), which does not reflect the intended in-game weighted-random behaviour (GDD §4.4) and cannot be tuned live.

## Users

- **Players / playtesters** — want the combat gyms to demonstrate power-up drops during genuine enemy pressure, so collection and effect behaviour (shield, bomb, phase, teleport, extra life, magnet) can be observed in context.
- **Game developers** — want a pluggable spawner plus a live-tunable game-rules config so spawn frequency and drop weights can be adjusted without editing scene code, and so the gyms reuse one shared implementation instead of per-scene copies.

### Example user stories

- As a playtester, I want power-ups to drop in the enemy and boss gyms so I can observe collection and effects while dodging real threats.
- As a developer, I want a live-tunable spawn-frequency control in the combat gyms so I can dial in the drop cadence without rebuilding.
- As a developer, I want the spawn ID selection and the spawn placement to be separate pluggable strategies so different scenes or difficulty tiers can swap either independently.
- As a developer, I want drop weights to follow the GDD rarity guidance (Extra Life rarer than standard drops) by default.

## Scope

**In scope:** `GymEnemies` (all archetypes) and `GymBoss`.

**Out of scope (already spawn, or enemy-free):** `GymPowerUps`, `GymPowerUpsCombat`, `GymWeapons`, `GymPlayer`, `GymIndex`. Converting these to the new random spawner/placement is a candidate follow-up, not part of this item.

## Existing state

- `src/powerups/spawner.ts` already provides the pluggable `PowerUpSpawner<T>` interface with `RoundRobinSpawner` and `WeightedRandomSpawner` (injectable RNG, runtime `setWeight`, equal initial weights) — the "pluggable spawner" seam already exists for ID selection.
- `src/powerups/PowerUp.ts` provides the shared grow → hold → shrink → despawn lifecycle and collection gating.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` (`EffectsRegistry`) tracks all active effects; `src/ui/HUD.ts` renders them (with a `showLives` option).
- `src/core/config.ts` is a localStorage-backed config system for `ShipConfig`, but there is **no** general game-rules config; power-up timing lives as hard-coded constants in `src/core/constants.ts` (`POWER_UP_SPAWN_INTERVAL = 12.5`).
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` is the shared base for `GymEnemies` and `GymBoss`; it has a `Player`, enemy entities/bullets and a wipe→respawn lifecycle, but no power-up layer and no HUD/`EffectsRegistry`.
- `GymPowerUpsCombat` is the reference implementation for combat-coupled collection (round-robin spawner, `EffectsRegistry`, P4 bullet clear, P7 teleport).

## Desired change

1. **General game-rules config** — new `src/core/rules.ts`, localStorage-backed and live-editable, mirroring the `src/core/config.ts` pattern (defaults merge, corrupt-JSON fallback). It holds the power-up spawn interval (default 12.5 s) and per-ID drop weights for P3–P9, defaulting to the GDD §4.4 rarity guidance (standard ~15–20 %, P8 Extra Life ~5 %, expressed as relative weights).
2. **Pluggable placement strategy** — new `src/powerups/placement.ts` exposing a `PowerUpPlacement` interface plus a `RandomAvoidingPlacement` implementation that chooses a random on-screen position (inside a margin) that does **not** overlap a live enemy body or the player, retries up to a configurable attempt limit, and then falls back to a deterministic safe position.
3. **Wire into the shared base** — `GymFormationScene` (covering both `GymEnemies` and `GymBoss`) gains an optional power-up layer: a `PowerUpSpawner` (default `WeightedRandomSpawner` over P3–P9 with the rules weights and an injectable RNG), the placement strategy, the shared `PowerUp` lifecycle, and drop tracking. One drop on screen at a time, next spawn on the configured interval.
4. **Full collection** — in both scenes, drops are fly-over collectible (≥ 3 % scale + hull overlap) and apply their effect through a shared `EffectsRegistry`; the standalone HUD renders active effects; P4 clears on-screen enemy bullets (no enemy damage), P7 is usable via S/↓ (nearest-safe-spot teleport + P6 on arrival), P8 updates the lives counter and P9 stacks.
5. **Live spawn-interval control** — a DOM-overlay slider (patterned on `GymPlayer`) edits the spawn interval in the running combat gym and persists it through the rules config.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1:** A new `src/core/rules.ts` exposes a general game-rules config containing the power-up spawn interval (default 12.5 s) and per-ID weights for P3–P9 (standard IDs equal, P8 Extra Life rarer, per GDD §4.4). Values load over defaults and persist via localStorage, with corrupt-JSON fallback. Unit tests cover defaults, round-trip, partial merge and corrupt fallback.
- [ ] **AC2 (testing/validation):** A pluggable `PowerUpPlacement` interface and `RandomAvoidingPlacement` implementation in `src/powerups/placement.ts` pick a random in-bounds position that does not overlap a live enemy body **or** the player, retry up to a configurable attempt limit, and return a deterministic safe fallback when no free position is found. Unit tests with an injected RNG verify non-overlap given supplied enemy/player positions, the retry path and the fallback path.
- [ ] **AC3:** `GymEnemies` (every archetype) and `GymBoss` spawn one power-up at a time on the configured interval, selecting the ID through a `PowerUpSpawner` (default `WeightedRandomSpawner` over P3–P9 with the rules weights) and positioning it through the placement strategy. Scene-level tests verify the spawn cadence and that spawned drops never overlap live enemies or the player.
- [ ] **AC4:** Spawned drops use the shared `PowerUp` lifecycle and are fly-over collectible (≥ 3 % scale + hull overlap); collecting applies the effect through a shared `EffectsRegistry` in both scenes. Tests cover at least one collectible path per scene.
- [ ] **AC5:** Both combat gyms render the standalone HUD for active effects; P4 clears on-screen enemy bullets without damaging enemies, P7 teleport works via S/↓, P8 updates the lives counter and P9 stacks. Tests verify each effect is observable in a combat gym.
- [ ] **AC6:** A live spawn-interval control in the combat gyms changes the spawn cadence of the running scene and persists the value through the rules config; a test covers live application and persistence.
- [ ] **AC7:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] **AC8:** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- No new runtime dependencies; reuse `PowerUpSpawner`, `PowerUp`, `EffectsRegistry`, `HUD`, `icons` and `audio` — do not fork existing implementations.
- Tests must be deterministic: inject the RNG used by the spawner and the placement strategy; never rely on the real render loop (drive scenes via `gameHarness`).
- The gym index and scene discovery must remain untouched — the shared base class carries the change to all archetypes.
- All written output in UK English.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption (confirmed):** "all combat gym scenes" means the enemy-bearing formation gyms `GymEnemies` and `GymBoss` only.
- **Assumption:** GDD §4.4 percentages are expressed as relative weights (for example standard = 4, P8 Extra Life = 1) rather than literal probabilities; the existing `WeightedRandomSpawner` semantics are reused unchanged.
- **Assumption:** "not on top of enemies" also excludes the player body, but proximity to the player is permitted (confirmed).
- **Assumption:** live edits apply immediately to the running scene; the next spawn uses the updated interval.
- **Risk:** adding an `EffectsRegistry`/HUD/drop layer to the shared `GymFormationScene` could regress existing `GymEnemies`/`GymBoss` behaviour — mitigate by wiring incrementally and running the full suite before review.
- **Risk (scope creep):** random placement + weighted spawning are also desirable in the three power-up/weapon gyms; this is recorded as a follow-up candidate rather than expanding this item.
- **Risk:** non-deterministic placement could make tests flaky — mitigate with injected, seeded RNGs.

- `src/core/rules.test.ts` — New unit tests for defaults, persistence, partial merge and corrupt fallback.
- `src/powerups/placement.ts` — New `PowerUpPlacement` interface and `RandomAvoidingPlacement` strategy.
- `src/powerups/placement.test.ts` — New unit tests for non-overlap, retry and fallback behaviour.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — Wire the spawner, placement strategy, drop lifecycle, collection, `EffectsRegistry` and HUD into the shared combat base.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts` — Extend with spawn-cadence, placement and collection tests.

- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts` — Enable and configure the power-up layer.

- `src/core/constants.ts` — Re-source or alias the power-up spawn-interval default from the new rules config.
- `README.md` — Document the combat gyms' power-up behaviour.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — Note the configurable/pluggable spawning for the combat gyms.

- `README.md` — gym scene documentation (adding a new gym scene / gym descriptions).
